analysis.title: "Metamorphic": Goldman's Pasquariello Sees One Last Push Higher, Then A 2027 Drowning In The Most Net Stock Supply Since 2000
key_insights: Pasquariello expects the S&P to make one last push higher before a turn, with 2027 a less rewarding year. He expects base index volatility to rise and the trading environment to favor flexible positioning.
He names three drivers of the market: earnings growth, the flow of capital and the AI narrative. He says all three now point the same way, toward worse conditions on the margin.

S&P earnings grew 33% in Q2 and Q3 is tracking 35%, the fastest pace in over 30 years outside post-recession recoveries. Growth is set to slow, and he cites 18% S&P EPS growth next year as still favorable for bulls historically.

Goldman's earnings forecast is very sensitive to AI capex, and the risks to it increased this week. He says it is increasingly hard to see earnings delivering the same upward convexity as in recent years.

Over the past three months the market absorbed a broad liquidation, which hit full tilt this week in global AI stocks. He describes a risk transfer from the trading community coinciding with a buyers' strike elsewhere.

Hedge fund demand inflected in mid-August and selling has been non-stop since, taking net exposure across Goldman's PB book to the lowest since March. On a trailing 20-day basis, hedge funds sold global AI stocks at the fastest pace in more than five years, about 3 standard deviations.

Households faded as buyers toward the end of summer and were net sellers in pockets this week. Corporate buybacks are constrained while large financings have cleared the market, which he calls perhaps the most significant turn.

He is relatively constructive on flows over the last eight weeks of 2026, and the desk notes buybacks are back at roughly $5 billion a day. He expects 2027 to see the largest increase in net stock supply since 2000, with a mega-IPO pipeline (SpaceX, Anthropic) and corporates needing cash for capex.

Big-five capex growth consensus slows from 96% this year to 44% next year. Hyperscalers burned $31 billion of free cash flow in Q3. Data center moratoria raised by the election outcome are described as arguably better for hyperscalers and worse for the rest of the AI infrastructure complex.

He sees more left tails in a market that was mostly chasing right tails, and less upside convexity in the picks-and-shovels part of the AI trade. If a slower buildout lengthens the cycle, medium-term optimism on the theme can be retained.

Privorotsky's counterpoint leans toward 1998 (a liquidity event and buying opportunity), arguing delayed data centers do not destroy compute demand. He concedes the parallel with 2000 in the scale of spending and uncertainty over returns.

Pasquariello says the market is now fairly valued after the de-rating. NDX and SOX trade at lower forward multiples than just before ChatGPT launched in late November 2022, about 4 turns cheaper, and NDX forward P/E is 18.4x, the lowest since 2020.
Healthcare became the second best performing sector YTD, attributed to defensive macro, strong EPS and flow of funds. European equities closed higher this week.
Two people he respects told him the stock market is far too sanguine relative to the credit market.

Context cited by the article: Nasdaq 100 fell 6.36% on Thursday, its worst day since Covid, and Friday payrolls of 165K were a 5-sigma beat that put a December hike back on the table. Goldman's TMT momentum pair lost two-thirds of its value since June highs (about 580 to 210). The article's authors, not Goldman, argue credit will be proven right first.

tension_points.bull_case: A slower buildout elongates the cycle and improves existing capacity economics. Privorotsky reads it as a 1998-style liquidity event and buying opportunity, and delaying data centers does not destroy compute demand.
tension_points.bear_case: Capex growth decelerates from 96% to 44% and hyperscalers burn cash, so earnings upside convexity falls and there are more left tails, especially in picks-and-shovels. Privorotsky concedes the 2000 parallel in scale of spending and uncertainty over returns.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Pasquariello says Goldman's earnings forecast is very sensitive to AI capex. A further cut to the pace of the buildout would break the bull case on earnings.

tension_points.bull_case: The primary trend remains intact, flows should improve over the last eight weeks of 2026, buybacks are back at about $5 billion a day, and the market is fairly valued at 18.4x NDX forward P/E.
tension_points.bear_case: Earnings growth is slowing, 2027 faces the largest net equity supply since 2000, and the AI buildout is at more risk than at any point in four years.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The turn would be confirmed if the S&P's last push higher fails before year-end and 2027 net supply arrives as expected.
